text:
maria: Quick thread — ran a focused benchmark on adaptive kernel routing with per-layer exclusion for embeddings + lm_head while KV cache is enabled. Saw weird tail-latency regressions on multi-turn chat sequences. TL;DR: throughput up on avg, but p99 jumps when KV cache warms and a few sensitive layers hit INT4 kernels.

ajohnson: Nice, can you paste the run config and perf numbers?
maria: gist of config below:
```
model: redwood-13b
quant: per_layer
exclude_layers: [embedding, lm_head]
adaptive_routing: true
routing_thresholds: {variance: 0.12, token_len: 64}
kv_cache: enabled
warmup: prefetch=32
fallback_policy: dynamic(fp8_on_miss_first_n=4)
```

maria: Results (avg of 5 runs):
- baseline float32: 420 tok/s
- int4 w/ exclude: 720 tok/s
- adaptive routing (this run): 680 tok/s (5% lower than static int4)
- p50/p95/p99 (adaptive): 1.6ms / 12.3ms / 48.9ms
- p99 spike correlated with KV warmup window and first-time layer kernel selection.

deepak: Hmm p99 that high is worrying. Any stack traces or kernel selection logs?
maria: Attached the short log excerpt where the selector flips kernels mid-request: 
```
[12:03:21.112] selector: layer_10 -> INT4 chosen (score 0.11)
[12:03:21.113] kv: miss -> warming, fetching prefix
[12:03:21.119] selector: layer_10 -> fallback to FP8 (latency penalty)
```

lucas: Is the fallback happening synchronously? If so that's the issue — kernel swap and KV fetch both blocking.
maria: Yes, in this experiment the routing decision happens at runtime on the forward pass and can trigger sync fallback. We tried async prefetch but it only helped when we knew the layer sequence (not for dynamic prompts).

keri: Could we bias routing to prefer FP8 for first 8 tokens after a KV miss, then re-evaluate? That would avoid repeated sync swaps.
ajohnson: Good idea. Also consider marking layers with high quantization error during calibration as "sticky-fp" so selector never picks INT4 for them.

maria: Did a quick follow-up with two mitigations: (1) sticky-fp on top-k sensitive layers, (2) async KV prefetch + early fp8 bias. Numbers:
- adaptive + mitigations: 705 tok/s, p99 18.7ms
- still ~2% below static int4 avg but p99 much better.

perf-bot: Profiling artifact uploaded: https://perf.redwood/reports/1965123456/adaptive-kernel-kv-warmup (contains per-layer time breakdown + nvprof traces) :white_check_mark:

qa-jen: Ran regression tests against our chat-e2e prompt set. Found one case where LM head exclusion caused a subtle logit shift for rare tokens in turn 5. Not a blocker but worth tracking.

deepak: Can you dump the calibration deltas for those sensitive layers? We need a threshold for automatic sticky-fp labeling.
maria: Uploaded calib diffs to the artifact. Quick rule-of-thumb I'm testing: mark layers with KL divergence > 0.018 during per-layer calibration as sticky-fp.

lucas: Also check memory live-sets — FP8 fallback increases KV memory temp usage which can evict other cached tensors and worsen tail. Might need a small in-memory reservation when fallback happens.

maria: Agreed. Next action items:
- maria: add sticky-fp heuristic and run 10-run stability sweep (in progress)
- deepak: add async prefetch + early-fp bias feature branch (PR by tomorrow)
- lucas: investigate reserving a small fallback pool to avoid cache evictions
- keri: add targeted eval for multi-turn rare-token drift (tracking ticket)

maria: One more note — we observed this only when prompts included long prefixes (>= 256 tokens) and KV cache churn rate was high (many unique keys). Short prompts not affected.

ajohnson: Makes sense. For hosted tier we could expose an opt-in `fallback_grace_tokens` knob that customers can tune per-route.

keri: Love that UX idea. Keep thread updated with the sweep results. :rocket:
